mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level is a positive predictor of S&P 500 forward 5-day returns, with higher rates consistently associated with positive returns. This is because the market views a higher rate as a sign of economic strength and reduced risk of recession, leading to increased equity valuations.
failure_condition: The rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 5-day forward returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 0.5% in the past 3 months, it signals a tightening monetary cycle that reduces equity risk premiums, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS has been above 0.5% for at least 3 months, 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) creates a predictive signal: when FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL is below 2.0% annually, it indicates a stable economic environment that supports positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising > 0.1% in last 3 months and CPIAUCSL < 2.0%
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.1% in last 3 months and CPIAUCSL < 2.0%) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.0% in the past 3 months, it signals an economic slowdown that leads to increased risk aversion and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as investors seek safe havens.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.0%, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 thousand units signals weak consumer demand and reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1200, 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 (2017=100) indicates strong economic growth, which leads to increased inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as the market prices in a potential monetary tightening.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 105, 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) creates a predictive signal: when HOUST is below 1200 and RSAFS is below 440,000 million dollars, it indicates a weak consumer demand environment that leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (HOUST < 1200 and RSAFS < 440000) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually), the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.0% signals a monetary policy response that reduces equity risk premiums, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 1.0%) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
